The Babolat Pure Drive 2025 sits at the top for you because it's built for exactly this: a player who can already generate pace and is looking for a racket that won't slow them down and won't ask their arm to do extra work. Its 300-gram weight and swingweight of 323 are on the higher end, which means more stability through the court and at net without excess overhead burden on the swing itself. The 16x19 string pattern is tight enough to give you spin control on aggressive groundstrokes while maintaining directional precision—critical for a baseliner whose game depends on consistency as much as power. The Wilson Ultra 100 v4 is slightly softer (RA 68) and a touch lighter in swingweight (318), tilting more toward comfort without abandoning performance. If that feels too demanding or expensive to restring regularly, RPM Blast 125 is a hybrid-friendly alternative that softens the transition and lasts longer. Start at 54 lbs—middle of the range—and adjust up or down in 2-pound increments based on how the frame's response feels to you in the first few hours.
